title: MtE Security under Restricted Leakage Sets
summary: A generic attack makes most MtE schemes insecure under general leakage; it remains open whether restricted leakage sets can yield security and exactly which restrictions suffice.

formal_statement.body: For MAC-then-Encrypt (MtE) schemes in a leakage setting, a generic attack applies to any scheme whose inversion follows either a decrypt-then-verify or a decrypt-and-verify structure, rendering most MtE schemes insecure under general leakage. Determine whether MtE schemes can be proven leakage-secure when the admissible leakage sets are more restricted than in the general setting, and characterize the precise conditions on the leakage sets under which such security can be achieved.

scope.domain: Leakage security of MAC-then-Encrypt authenticated-encryption schemes.
parameters: Admissible leakage sets — their restrictions govern the sought leakage-security characterization
Inversion structure — decrypt-then-verify or decrypt-and-verify enables the generic attack
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether restricted leakage sets permit provable leakage security for MtE schemes and characterize the precise restrictions under which security is achievable.

citations.label: Authenticated Encryption in the Face of Protocol and Side Channel Leakage

progress.summary: The source attributes the insecurity of most MtE schemes under leakage to a generic attack on decrypt-then-verify and decrypt-and-verify inversion structures. It explicitly leaves leakage security under more restricted leakage sets as an open question.
citation_labels: Guy Barwell et al., Authenticated Encryption in the Face of Protocol and Side Channel Leakage
